title: Upgrading a 1944 bungalow shower to a modern pressure-balanced valve with minimal demolition

locations.name: Salt Lake City, Utah (probable job site)
locations.basis: The host explicitly references Salt Lake City as where the fix takes place at the end of the segment.

summary: This Old House profiles a pragmatic retrofit of a decades-old two-valve shower in a 1944 bungalow. With a leaking valve and a reluctance to rip out the surround, the crew upgrades to a modern single-lever, pressure-balanced valve behind the existing fiberglass. The process includes identifying the old valve type, fabricating access by removing a kitchen cabinet and scoring a remodel plate, uncovering galvanized piping behind the wall, replacing the run with copper, soldering joints outside the wall, and carefully threading the new connections back into place. A raised shower arm, a cockhole cover to conceal an old hole, and a cover plate with a diverter complete the tub-to-shower functionality while keeping the wall intact. The video also discusses copper versus PEX and how to anchor piping to studs to prevent movement, ending with a test of the new system by the homeowners.
topics: blocking between studs to secure pipes

sections.title: Problem statement and valve basics
sections.description: The homeowners describe a leaking shower valve and an oversized repair quote. The host identifies the vintage, two-valve arrangement and explains that it predates single-lever pressure-balanced designs, which use an internal balancing spool to prevent scalding during pressure changes.

concepts: remodel plate that covers a larger opening
why a standard plate won’t cover the old opening
sections.description: Discussion of a manufacturer’s remodeling plate designed to cover a larger opening and allow access to a modern valve without tearing out the fiberglass surround.

sections.title: Access planning and structural layout
concepts: kitchen cabinet removal to reach back of wall
using an access panel and remodeling plate together
sections.description: The team considers opening the wall via the kitchen cabinet to gain full access to the back of the shower wall and to facilitate the new valve installation.

sections.title: Discovery and material strategy
sections.description: An exposed section reveals galvanized steel plumbing behind the wall, prompting a copper piping plan and avoidance of limited access for threading two wrenches.

sections.title: Valve installation workflow
concepts: dropping the valve assembly into the wall
sections.description: The crew drops the new valve assembly into the prepared opening, centers it, and begins the tub spout connection with careful measurement.

sections.title: Shower arm height and height adjustment
concepts: drilling a new height for the shower arm
using a cockhole cover to block the old hole
sections.description: A new shower arm height is established, and a cockhole cover is used to conceal the previous opening, with the arm temporarily threaded into place during fit-up.

sections.title: Final plumbing assembly and diverter integration
concepts: blocking between studs to prevent pipe banging
diverter dial in the cover plate
connecting hot and cold from basement
sections.description: The team blocks and secures the piping, installs the cover plate with a built-in diverter to switch between tub spout and shower head, uses a gasket in place of caulk, and completes the hot/cold connections from the basement.

sections.title: Testing, materials choice, and don’t-hesitate tips
concepts: use of a copper 'tree' to anchor inside wall
sections.description: Final test shows the new pressure-balanced valve functioning properly. The host discusses copper versus PEX, favoring copper for a rigid internal branching tree and easier anchoring, and wraps with guidance and a plug for subscribing.

featured_techniques.technique: Install a modern single-lever, pressure-balanced shower valve behind an existing fiberglass wall using a remodeling/cover plate design
Create an access pathway through the kitchen wall by removing a cabinet and cutting an opening for back-side plumbing work
Expose galvanized piping behind the wall and plan to replace with copper due to age and corrosion risk
Pre-assemble solder connections outside the wall to simplify installation, then slide the assembly into place
Drill a higher shower-arm hole and use a cockhole cover to conceal the old hole while maintaining a clean finish
Integrate a diverter dial into the cover plate to switch between tub spout and shower head
Anchor and block piping between studs to minimize movement and banging when the water runs
Use a gasket on the cover plate to avoid caulking and ensure a tight seal
